findings.claim: complexity-gate's comment said a skipped path is named 'so an accidental rm is not "fixed" with --update-baseline', but nothing enforced it. For an unstaged rm of a baselined file the stale-row refusal printed --update-baseline as the fix, and following it exited 0 and dropped the ceilings of a file HEAD and the index still track, so the committed tip goes red on a clean checkout. The pin vanished-source-silent checked only that the note printed. Independently rediscovered by lanes 3, 5, 6 and 7 (lane 7: the pin tests a smaller claim than the comment makes).

findings.claim: The repair turns a red HEAD into a green gate: a committed file that violates test-lint or complexity-gate is hidden by deleting it from disk without staging the deletion. The skip rests on 'content equals HEAD, judged when it landed', which the repo does not guarantee (WIRING: no local hook runs the battery). Before the fix this state crashed on ENOENT (exit 1); after it both tools exit 0, advance verified keeps no stderr of a green run, and only CI on the pushed tip catches it. No pin covers a skip that hides a HEAD-red file.

findings.justification: Not restored to fail-closed, on measurement. (1) The class predates this change and is wider than this spelling: a committed violation is already hidden from these working-tree tools by editing its disk copy without staging. At 4802b45, before this task, a committed 10-branch tools/zz-bad.mjs rewritten clean on disk gives 'complexity-gate: OK ... nothing new born convoluted'. The ENOENT crash closed only the deletion spelling, by accident, and at the cost this task exists to remove: every legitimate uncommitted git rm or git mv read INCONCLUSIVE in guard-reach and blocked advance verified. (2) Judging the index blob instead is the design's rejected alternative: under guard-reach's HEAD-index baseline it re-scans a git rm'd file whose baseline rows the author removed and reports it born convoluted. (3) The premise is no longer claimed: 0716358 removes 'judged when it landed' from both docstrings, and WIRING now states that neither tool re-reads what a commit carries but the disk does not show (HEAD's content for a skipped path, a committed file edited without staging, staged-then-edited content) and that only a clean-clone run (CI on the pushed tip) judges it. Closing the class means judging the index or HEAD tree instead of the working tree in both tools, which is a separate design decision and not this repair.

findings.claim: listedOnDisk sorted a path into `skipped` on a weaker test than its message and WIRING stated: it checks only absence from `git diff --cached`, never that HEAD holds the path or that it is tracked, yet printed 'tracked path(s) missing from disk (content equals HEAD)'. An untracked dangling symlink (complexity-gate lists --others) and a deleted intent-to-add entry (git add -N; HEAD lacks it) both got that false label; the self-test doubles covered only a committed-then-deleted regular file. Independently rediscovered by lane 5 (the intent-to-add case).

findings.justification: Fence surface. docs/gates/guard-reach.json is under FENCE_SURFACE (tools/task-state.mjs), so recording the reason there would make this runtime-code task protected-tier and need an owner approval; the approved design answered its open question 4 with 'not in guard-reach.json in this task'. The gap cannot become an escape: if doc-reconcile were ever registered alongside a repo-count claim, its refusal on a vanished tracked file makes guard-reach's own baseline run report INCONCLUSIVE, which blocks instead of passing. 0716358 rewrites the WIRING paragraph to say the caveat lives only there, that the registry records the edit-probe reason alone, and that amending it is fence surface, so no reader is told the registry carries it. A guard-reach.json edit can follow under a protected task if the owner wants it.

findings.claim: The commit subject promises to 'refuse staged content the disk lacks', but only staged-then-DELETED refuses. Staged-then-EDITED has the same outcome (the index holds content the disk does not, and the commit carries it unread) and still exits 0, because listedOnDisk consults `git diff --cached` only for paths missing from disk; the same commit writes that case into WIRING and test-lint's header as a boundary. Pre-existing. Independently rediscovered by lane 8.

findings.justification: A boundary that predates this change, kept on purpose and now stated precisely. Refusing whenever a present file's index blob differs from both HEAD and the disk would refuse every partial-staging state (git add -p), which is exactly the state a vendor's pre-commit hook runs these tools in. Reading the index blob for present files would, in complexity-gate, judge index text against a working-tree baseline and bring back the false red the ponytail note records. Both tools judge the working tree, and 0716358 states in WIRING and in test-lint's header that staged content under a file since edited is not re-read and that only a clean-clone run judges it. The 4cd41db subject line is recorded history and is not rewritten; the accurate scope (a missing path with a staged change refuses) is what the code, the header and WIRING now say.

findings.claim: `--relative` on the `git diff --cached` call is load-bearing and was unpinned: run from a subdirectory without it, the staged set holds root-relative names while ls-files gives cwd-relative ones, so staged-then-deleted content is skipped (exit 0) instead of refused. Deleting `--relative` from either tool left both self-tests green.
